Practice pillars — what I prioritize

Clarity over jargon

You’ll get plain language and concrete steps — not buzzwords. Therapy should feel logical and understandable.

Collaboration

We set shared goals and track progress. Your values direct the pace and focus.

Practical change

Each session includes a small experiment to try between meetings — useful and measurable.

Tools I draw on

I tailor approaches to what you need in-session and between sessions. Typical elements include:

  • Cognitive Behavioral techniques for shifting unhelpful patterns
  • Trauma-informed grounding and pacing
  • Interpersonal work for communication and boundaries
  • Executive coaching-style planning for life transitions and career stress

Modality note: {{MODALITIES}}

Hesitations I hear — and how we handle them

"I don't know if therapy will help me."

We start with a brief roadmap and small, measurable tasks. If you don’t feel benefit in an agreed period, we revisit the plan together.

"I’m worried about confidentiality."

Confidentiality is fundamental. I’ll explain limits to confidentiality, record-keeping, and how I protect your privacy in our first meeting.

"I’m too busy for weekly sessions."

We can design shorter check-ins, a limited series, or a hybrid of in-person and remote meetings to fit your schedule.

"Will you judge me?"

My work is nonjudgmental and pragmatic. We focus on what’s effective for you, not on blame.

Client reflections

"I left each session with something concrete to practice. After three months I felt more grounded in my work and relationships."
"The clarity and structure made it easier to take risks. I appreciated the direct but warm approach."

Focused care

Clinical specialties — what I work with most often

Evidence-informed, client-centered support for adults struggling with daily functioning, relationships, and the ongoing stressors of modern life.

{{PRIMARY_CTA_LABEL}}

Anxiety & Worry

Short-term strategies for panic and persistent worry, plus longer-term cognitive work to reduce avoidance and rebuild confidence.

  • Generalized anxiety
  • Social anxiety
  • Panic symptoms

Trauma-Informed Care

Stabilization and paced processing; we prioritize safety, regulation, and choice over intensity.

  • Complex stress responses
  • Boundaries & relationships impacted by trauma

Relationship & Communication

Practical skills for clearer expression, problem-solving, and boundary-setting — for partners and individuals.

Life Transitions & Career Strain

Decisions about work, direction, and identity with structured planning and values clarification.

Burnout & Overwhelm

Assessment of limits, recovery planning, and small habit changes to reclaim bandwidth without sacrificing goals.

Parenting Stress & Role Shifts

Support for parents and caregivers navigating identity, boundaries, and relationship strain during life changes.

How work differs by need

Treatment is matched to the presenting problem. For example:

  • Anxiety: behavioral experiments and exposure in bite-sized steps
  • Trauma: pacing, grounding, and titrated memory work when appropriate
  • Relationships: communication exercises and role-based practice

Modalities include: {{MODALITIES}}

Is my concern "big enough" for therapy?

Therapy is for persistent patterns, not just crises. If a problem repeatedly disrupts your life or drains energy, it’s worth exploring. We’ll define a target together and set realistic measures of improvement.

What people say

"Working on small exposure tasks helped me leave a job I was stuck in with more clarity and less anxiety."
"We built a plan for weekend recovery rituals that actually worked — my energy improved within weeks."

Quick toolkit

Download a short set of tools for acute anxiety and overwhelm — exercises you can use immediately.

Get the Toolkit

Foundations Series

6 sessions focused on stabilization and skills building.

Momentum Track

12-week plan for deeper change with measurable checkpoints.

Intensive Reset

Short, concentrated support for major transitions. (Limited availability)

Home Areas Who I am Contact

A clear path — predictable steps, flexible pacing

My approach blends assessment, structured skill building, and review. We treat therapy as a series of small experiments, not vague promises.

How we organize the work

1. Intake & goal-setting

A focused first session to identify priorities, safety needs, and what success looks like for you.

2. Skill-building & practice

Short, practical tools between sessions and in-session rehearsal to build confidence.

3. Review & adjustment

Regular checkpoints to measure progress, refine goals, and shift strategy if needed.

Coaching-infused psychotherapeutic stance

  • Agency-focused: you choose targets and pace.
  • Skill-first: we practice concrete behaviors rather than only talk.
  • Evidence-aware: I use techniques with a clear rationale and an eye toward measurable change.

Practical questions — scheduling, pacing, and telehealth

How long before I notice a change?

People often report small improvements in weeks when they regularly practice skills. Meaningful, sustained change depends on the goal and consistency.

What if I can't commit weekly?

We design a cadence that fits your life — fortnightly sessions, brief check-ins, or intensive blocks are options.

Do you take insurance?

I offer private-pay sessions and can provide superbills. Insurance terms vary; contact me for current details.

On the process

"I appreciated the structure — each session had a purpose and next steps. That made progress feel real."
"The clarity call helped me decide to commit. I felt seen and understood from the start."

Get a 20-minute clarity call

A short conversation to identify priorities and determine fit — no obligation.

Book the clarity call

Next step

If your concerns involve imminent danger to self or others, call emergency services. For outpatient support, schedule a clarity call to discuss fit and logistics.
